rejected_videos.reason: Reject for technical inaccuracy and prerequisite-unsafe setup. At 353–355, the video incorrectly describes CollectD as collecting logging information for the CloudWatch agent; collectd supplies metrics, while the agent's log-file collection sends logs. The catalogue chapters also disagree materially with the transcript: 5–207 concerns network load balancing, and CloudWatch-agent instruction starts at 210. The subsequent setup teaches blocked instance-profile configuration (309–310), Systems Manager Run Command (326–348), and log retention (396). The wizard demonstration depends on an external course document and earlier installation, does not explicitly explain metrics_collected or InstanceId, and references commands by document line number without establishing amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl fetch-config, the supplied configuration location, or -s in the transcript. The final verification at 428–473 supports agent delivery of metrics and logs but does not verify an instance-identifying dimension. No clean, technically reliable standalone setup-and-verification segment meets this path's bounded procedure.

Reject for technical inaccuracies and prerequisite/boundary problems. At 140–165, the instructor adds an inbound HTTPS security-group rule and incorrectly presents it as necessary for CloudWatch-agent communication; the agent sends telemetry using outbound connections. At 284–297, StatsD is incorrectly described as responsible for fetching all activity data, rather than receiving application-emitted custom metrics. The setup also teaches blocked EC2 instance-profile configuration (36–112), security-group configuration (140–165), and log retention (468–478). No clean standalone range demonstrates the required supplied-configuration procedure through metric verification without these dependencies: the start command at 532–560 is referenced only as an on-screen command, so the transcript does not establish amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl, fetch-config, the configuration location, or -s. The metric-inspection portion can reinforce InstanceId-specific output, but cannot substantiate the complete required procedure on its own.

Although 305–586 provides a potentially useful complete-data window example, the subsequent missing-data explanation introduces simplified sparse-data behavior without establishing the required default-missing behavior when all datapoints are missing. No clean standalone segment teaches the required recovery controls. The demonstration configures current-version storage transitions and expiration, not version inspection, delete-marker handling, restoration, or noncurrent-version retention for a required recovery window. Its brief versioning explanation at 145–159 seconds misleadingly implies versions are retained whenever a file is modified, without requiring versioning to be enabled. At 249–281 seconds, it describes current-version expiration as deleting the object outright; in a versioning-enabled bucket, current-version expiration ordinarily creates a delete marker rather than permanently removing retained versions. These are factual problems for this concept, not merely coverage gaps.
